study.question: Observation: baseline-static/pooled/din have validation AUC 0.6050036145/0.6102261137/0.6133619861. The prior compressed-history factorial yields target_directional 0.6114152265, target_scalar 0.6100255150, context_directional 0.6098765382 and context_scalar 0.6089084234. Target and direction contrasts are positive within that family, but all four lose to baseline-din. Can current-ad category and brand independently select event-level evidence at fixed summary norm more effectively than requiring consensus on the same events, and does any gain require the current target? Prior compression, gates, head width and optimization changed together, so information loss from compression is a provisional explanation only.
study.hypothesis: Category and brand may express useful interests through different events. Averaging their scores before a shared softmax creates a consensus bottleneck; separate field softmaxes can retrieve complementary events while retaining every supplied category/brand/action/age tuple. The effect should depend on current-ad queries and should remain when the final summary norm is fixed to the target-independent masked-mean history norm. This changes event selection and field-value fusion, rather than channel gating over action-level means. No causal attribution of the previous DIN gap to compression and no priority/novelty claim is made.

nearest_work.difference: Primary archived v4 text, source-text://paper:din lines 250-277, text SHA256 83fb9eeca31e2fa3c557b6f08b893ad0018cefb33da6e00952136b9ce17e607e. Inherit target-conditioned weighted history and query/key/product relations. Original DIN deliberately omits softmax to retain interest intensity; the local reference already uses softmax and is not an exact reproduction. This experiment uses two field-specific softmaxes versus a shared consensus softmax and an explicit target-independent summary-norm control. These are local controlled differences, not established novelty.

Read candidate.py and baseline_reference.py before editing; both match the supplied reference. It scores summed category+brand+action+recency with a summed target category+brand query and produces one d-vector. New variants preserve its parameter shapes and output width but use two shared-scorer field relations and normalize to the pooled-history norm. Comparison to baseline is an overall quality/cost bridge, not a single-factor attribution.

Read history_g2_r0000_target_directional.py and all four authorized receipts from run://r-001. Prior work selects 2x4 field/action means and uses channel gates with two d-vector outputs. New work preserves event granularity, removes gates and extra output width, and contrasts two selection/fusion rules at the same d-vector norm. A better new result alone would not prove that compression caused the old deficit.

study.proposed_difference: For event t define c_t, b_t and a_t=action_t+age_t. A shared scorer produces s_c,t=f(q_c,c_t+a_t), s_b,t=f(q_b,b_t+a_t). Target queries are current category/brand embeddings; context controls use masked means of past category/brand embeddings, without current-ad input to routing. Separate readout: w_c=softmax_mask(s_c), w_b=softmax_mask(s_b), z_sep=sum_t[w_c,t*c_t+w_b,t*b_t+0.5*(w_c,t+w_b,t)*a_t]. Consensus control: w_j=softmax_mask(0.5*(s_c+s_b)), z_joint=sum_t[w_j,t*(c_t+b_t+a_t)]. Both are rescaled to ||mean_mask(c+b+a)||_2, with reference-vector fallback for raw norm <=1e-6. Empty histories yield zero; singleton histories make both raw readouts identical. No action compression, learned channel gate, new parameters, loss or optimizer. All four standalone modules evaluate both paths; config selects target/context x separate/consensus. The consensus control is a field-factorized replacement, not byte-identical baseline-din. No standalone amplitude gain claim follows from the normalization constraint.
predictions: Primary: target_separate exceeds target_consensus in full-population validation AUC under the same seed/recipe. Reference margin of practical interest is +0.0005 AUC, not a significance threshold.

Target relevance: target_separate exceeds context_separate. Stronger target-specific complementarity evidence requires positive interaction (AUC(target_separate)-AUC(target_consensus))-(AUC(context_separate)-AUC(context_consensus)); a zero interaction limits the claim to target-independent factorization.

Practical success requires target_separate to exceed baseline-din AUC 0.6133619861 as well as the matched controls; report Logloss and measured cost even if ranking differs. A control may remain the best model.

Candidate-supplied first-512-impression diagnostics should show nonzero category/brand weight disagreement and nonidentical separate/joint directions, with maximum relative norm error near floating-point precision (inspect if >1e-4) and no empty-history contribution. Context controls must have zero weight change versus context queries.

Exploratory existing slices: report all host slices with sample/positive/negative counts, especially history_gt64 (3026583 samples, 151372 positives, 2875211 negatives) and category_match_present (2516922 samples, 129821 positives, 2387101 negatives). Existing bins are frozen; these predictions follow observed data and are not independent confirmatory evidence.
falsifiers: No target_separate advantage over target_consensus rejects the proposed benefit of separate field selection for this implementation/recipe; it does not refute all independent attention mechanisms.
A separate-read advantage equally present with context queries, or failure to beat context_separate, does not support target-specific complementarity.
Failure to exceed baseline-din leaves the practical research objective unachieved even if a factorial contrast is positive. Preserve a successful incumbent.

Collapsed field weights, almost identical separate/consensus directions or invariant routing when replacing target with context contradict the proposed retrieval explanation; first-512 diagnostics alone are insufficient to establish population behavior.

Nonfinite output, nonzero empty-history summary, systematic norm mismatch >1e-4 relative error outside degeneracies, or high nonempty fallback use is an implementation/numerical issue requiring a charged corrective run before a directional interpretation.
If paired seeds reverse the AUC contrasts or Logloss degrades consistently, evidence remains unstable or metric-specific; no general superiority claim.
alternative_explanations: The previous four compressed variants change tokenization, gates, classifier width and training dynamics together. The new suite cannot retrospectively isolate the cost of compression.

Separate attention can help by reducing score sharpness or changing score scale rather than retrieving complementary semantic evidence. Inspect entropy alongside field disagreement; a future temperature/score-scale control is needed if entropy alone explains the difference.

Shared scorer inductive bias, different target/context query distributions, embedding norm learning or fixed-norm gradient dynamics can explain a result. Equal parameter counts do not imply equal optimization difficulty, and Euclidean norm matching does not fix per-coordinate classifier sensitivity.
One-seed selection noise, validation adaptation and repeated user exposures can explain small improvements. Aggregate slice differences do not independently establish a mechanism.
Most validation exposures have histories >64 events, and exposure slices overlap by user. Broad averages may obscure rare/empty-history harm; first-512 diagnostics may be unrepresentative.
Baseline quality gap may reflect intensity information deliberately removed by the norm control. A future norm-restoration contrast would be required; do not relax this control mid-suite.

cost_plan.stop_rule: All preparation, source diagnostics, model diagnostics, failures, retries and final assessments count under the host ledger. Never exceed the fixed 1760.9324 s per-trial cap or remaining total. Stop or submit fewer admissible future experiments when no complete unit fits after reserves; do not raise limits or auto-retry unknown execution states. No significance, mechanism success or practical improvement is inferred before host scores. If all new variants lose to baseline-din, preserve the null result; pursue a later single discriminating change only if diagnostics and remaining budget justify it.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Read primary arxiv:2609.16548v1 query pipeline, lines 128-181. Field-to-history retrieval is existing work, but prior local factorial outcomes do not establish a query-generation bottleneck. Source pCVR/multi-domain scale and split differ.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: No generated-query pipeline adopted. Direct field queries and the history-only replacement follow the available category/brand inputs and local DIN reference.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: One shared shallow relation scorer, event-level category/brand keys, separate-versus-consensus softmax and explicit norm matching; no refined query probes, multiple views or bridge stack. Novelty remains unverified.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: Failure of target-query contrasts weakens the local need for target-aware routing; it is not a test of QueryFormer itself.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Retrieved organizer-only card lacks original implementation and full ablations. All four previous action-mean variants lose to DIN, but this does not establish the value or failure of the source token allocation.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: No learned token allocation or gated decoder adopted. Keep every supplied history event and a fixed d-dimensional output; investigate field-readout rules through local controls.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: No joint field projections or learned token budget. Detailed primary-source comparison remains unavailable; no reproduction or priority claim.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: A local loss of separate event readout rejects only this implementation, not the external tokenization method.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Read primary arxiv:2608.16797v1 lines 163-206 and review prior knowledge-usage declarations against all four executed g2-r0000 outcomes. The declared channel-gate adaptation shows positive within-family directional contrasts but best AUC 0.6114152265 trails DIN 0.6133619861. This is preliminary evidence for the local controlled contrasts, not confirmation of UniDot transfer or its FM Highway.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: No UniDot-specific component adopted in the new suite. Remove prior gates and compressed action means; study separate field event retrieval at fixed history norm.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: No dual buses, recurrent per-layer interaction, FM Highway, conditional SwiGLU, mutual learning, auxiliary labels or optimizer changes. Event-readout factorial remains a local adaptation of established target-aware attention.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: A failure of the new suite does not refute UniDot; target/context and separate/consensus contrasts test only their explicit local mechanisms.
